name: D-serine
short: High doses damage the kidneys in rats; in human studies one participant had abnormal kidney values, which resolved after stopping. A 16-week low-dose trial reported it was well tolerated.
text: A systematic review of D-serine safety reported that kidney toxicity (acute tubular necrosis) is highly common in rats given doses above 500 mg/kg, is dose dependent and reversible, and has not been reported in other animal species. Across all published human studies, the review found only one participant with abnormal kidney values related to D-serine, which fully resolved within a few days of stopping treatment; the review found no other clinically significant safety concerns and concluded that D-serine appears safe at the highest doses studied so far, under kidney monitoring. In a 16-week placebo-controlled trial in 195 people with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder taking antipsychotics, D-serine at 2 g per day, which the trial's title calls low-dose, was reported to be well tolerated; the authors noted that the doses achieved were somewhat lower than in prior studies. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
